{{short description|German mathematician}}
'''Maria-Pia Geppert''' (May 28, 1907 – November 18, 1997) was a German mathematician and [[biostatistics|biostatistician]] who co-founded the ''[[Biometrical Journal]]''.{{r|dietz}}

Geppert was the first woman to become a full professor at the [[University of Tübingen]].{{r|leo}}
With [[Emmy Noether]], [[Hilda Geiringer]], [[Ruth Moufang]], and [[Hel Braun]], Geppert was one of only a handful of women to work in mathematics in Germany before World War II and later convert their degrees into research careers as full professors.{{r|dumsch}}

==Early life and education==
Geppert was born in [[Breslau]], with Italian descent through her mother. Breslau is now [[Wrocław]], in Poland, but at that time it was part of the [[German Empire]]. Her older brother, {{ill|Harald Geppert|de}} also became a mathematician, and a supporter of the Nazis.{{r|mun}}

She studied mathematics in Breslau and in [[Giessen]],{{r|dietz}} and in 1932 completed a doctorate at the [[University of Breslau]]. Her dissertation, ''Approximative Darstellungen analytischer Funktionen, die durch Dirichletsche Reihen gegeben sind'', concerned [[analytic number theory]] and was supervised by [[Guido Hoheisel]].{{r|mgp}} [[Edmund Landau]], in his last publication before Hitler came to power, commented unfavorably on one of her papers.{{r|mun}}

Next, Geppert moved to Rome, where from 1933 to 1936 she studied [[actuarial science]] and [[statistics]] for a second doctorate under the supervision of [[Guido Castelnuovo]].{{r|dietz}}
She completed a [[habilitation]] in 1942 at the [[University of Giessen]]. Her dissertation was ''Comparison of Two Observed Frequencies''.{{r|dietz}}
{{harvtxt|Seneta|Phipps|2001}} write that her habilitation dissertation was "important but forgotten" because of the circumstances of the war, and they adopt her title for their own.{{r|sp01}}

==Career==
In 1940, Geppert became director of the Department of Epidemiology and Statistics for the William G. Kerckhoff Heart Research Institute in [[Bad Nauheim]], later to become the [[Max Planck Institute for Heart and Lung Research]].{{r|dietz|mpi}} She joined [[Goethe University Frankfurt]] in 1943, as a lecturer in biostatistics.{{r|dietz}}

In 1964 she became chair for medical biometry at the [[University of Tübingen]].{{r|dietz}} In doing so, she became the first female full professor at the University of Tübingen.{{r|leo}}
She retired in 1975.{{r|leo}}

==''Biometrical Journal''==
With Ottokar Heinisch, Geppert founded the ''[[Biometrical Journal]]'' in 1959. She was co-editor-in-chief with Heinisch from its founding until 1966, and remained co-editor-in-chief with {{ill|Erna Weber|de}} until 1969.{{r|dietz}}

==Recognition==
In 1951, Geppert became the first German elected into the [[International Statistical Institute]] in the post-war period.{{r|dietz}} She also became an honorary member of the [[International Biometric Society]] in 1965, the first person from the German region of the society to be so honored.{{r|dietz|leo|ibs}}
